title: Wedding of Nicolas Sarkozy and Carla Bruni.
text: Nicolas Paul Stéphane Sarközy de Nagy-Bocsa is a French former politician who served as the president of the French Republic from 2007 to 2012. Sarkozy was born in Paris.

title: Cantonal elections held.
text: Cantonal elections to elect half the membership of the general councils of France's 100 departments were held on 9 and 16 March 2008. These elections coincided with the municipal elections, in which the left did well.

title: Lazare Ponticelli, the country's last surviving First World War veteran, dies aged 110 – eight months before the 90th anniversary of the Armistice.
text: Lazare Ponticelli, Knight of Vittorio Veneto, was at 110, the last surviving officially recognized veteran of the First World War from France and the last poilu of its trenches to die. Born in Italy, he travelled on his own to France at the age of eight.

title: The Citroën C5 sedan is launched, whilst the station wagon was launched in May.
text: The Citroën C5 is a large family car produced by the French manufacturer Citroën between 2000 and 2018 in France, and between 2008 and 2022 in China, over two generations. It replaced the Citroën Xantia, in the large family car class, and is the first modern Citroën with "Cx" naming nomenclature, previously used by its ancestors, the C4 and C6 from 1930.

title: 2008 French mistaken virginity case
text: On 1 April 2008, the high court of Lille annulled a marriage on the grounds of "mistaken essential qualities of the spouse" in accordance with article 180 paragraph 2 of the French civil code. The woman was not a virgin at the time of the marriage ceremony, but had not admitted this to the man even though she knew that her status as a virgin was a determining factor in his motivation and consent to marry her.

title: France assumes the Presidency of the Council of the European Union.
text: The presidency of the Council of the European Union is responsible for the functioning of the Council of the European Union, which is the co-legislator of the EU legislature alongside the European Parliament. It rotates among the member states of the EU every six months.
wiki: Presidency of the Council of the European Union

title: Íngrid Betancourt and 14 other hostages are rescued from FARC by Colombian security forces.
text: Íngrid Betancourt Pulecio is a Colombian-French politician, former senator, and anti-corruption activist. She gained international prominence after being kidnapped by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) in 2002 while campaigning for the Colombian presidency as a Green candidate.

title: First meeting of Mediterranean Union, in Paris
text: The Union for the Mediterranean is an intergovernmental organization of 43 member states from Europe and the Mediterranean basin: all 27 European Union member states (including those not on the Mediterranean) and 16 Mediterranean partner countries from North Africa, Southern Europe, and West Asia. The UfM was founded on 13 July 2008 at the Paris Summit for the Mediterranean, with the aim of reinforcing the Euro-Me…

title: Activation of Large Hadron Collider, localized between France and Switzerland
text: The Large Hadron Collider is the world's largest and highest-energy particle accelerator. It was built by the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN) between 1998 and 2008, in collaboration with over 10,000 scientists, and hundreds of universities and laboratories across more than 100 countries.

title: 50th Anniversary of the French Constitution of 1958 (French Fifth Republic).
text: The current Constitution of France was adopted on 4 October 1958. It is typically called the Constitution of the Fifth Republic, and it replaced the Constitution of the Fourth Republic of 1946, keeping its preamble.

title: XL Airways Germany Flight 888T crashed on a Mediterranean Sea, near Canet-en-Roussillon around Perpignan, killed seven people.
text: XL Airways Germany Flight 888T was an acceptance flight for an Airbus A320 on 27 November 2008. The aircraft crashed into the Mediterranean Sea, 7 km off Canet-en-Roussillon on the French coast, close to the Spanish border, killing all seven people on board.

title: Françoise Barré-Sinoussi and Luc Montagnier – the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
text: Françoise Barré-Sinoussi is a French virologist and Director of the Regulation of Retroviral Infections Division (French: Unité de Régulation des Infections Rétrovirales) and Professor at the Institut Pasteur in Paris. Born in Paris, Barré-Sinoussi performed some of the fundamental work in the identification of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) as the cause of AIDS. title: – First album of the series Je n'aime pas le classique, mais ça j'aime bien! was released
text: Je n'aime pas le classique, mais ça j'aime bien! is a successful series of compilation albums of classical music interpreted by various artists.

title: Black music, des chaînes de fer aux chaînes d'or documentary film is released.
text: Black music, des chaînes de fer aux chaînes d'or is a French 2008 documentary film about African-American music.

title: Yeallow, French indie rock band from Strasbourg is formed.
text: Yeallow is a French indie rock band from Strasbourg, Alsace, formed in 2008.

text: Frédéric Forestier, né le 8 février 1969 à Paris, est un réalisateur français.

title: Il divo, film italien de Paolo Sorrentino.
text: Le cinéma italien, qui est le cinéma produit ou réalisé en Italie, est l'un des principaux cinémas nationaux de l'histoire du cinéma. L’histoire du cinéma italien a commencé quelques mois après que les frères Lumière eurent présenté au public leur appareil original, le Cinématographe, le 28 décembre 1895 à Paris : ce sont eux qui l'introduisent en Italie au cours de l'année 1896.

title: César du meilleur film : La Graine et le Mulet, - d'Abdellatif Kechiche
text: Le César du meilleur film est une récompense cinématographique française décernée par l'Académie des arts et techniques du cinéma depuis la première remise de prix le 3 avril 1976 au Palais des congrès à Paris.

title: Prix Jean-Vigo : Nulle part, terre promise, d'Emmanuel Finkiel
text: Le prix Jean-Vigo est une récompense cinématographique française décernée depuis 1951.

title: “Parle à ma main”
text: "Parle à ma main" is a song recorded by French act Fatal Bazooka featuring Yelle and released on October 15, 2007. It was the fifth and last single from the album T'as vu.

title: “Il avait les mots”
text: "II avait les mots" is a pop music song recorded by contemporary R&B singer Sheryfa Luna, on the topic of relationships and infidelity. It was her second single from her debut album entitled Sheryfa Luna.

title: “Bleeding Love”
text: "Bleeding Love" is a song recorded by British singer Leona Lewis for her debut studio album, Spirit. It was originally written and recorded by American singer Jesse McCartney, and was co-written and produced by American singer Ryan Tedder.

title: “Dangerous”
text: "Dangerous" is the first single from French singer M. Pokora's third album MP3. The song was produced by Timbaland and features Timbaland and his younger brother, Sebastian.

title: “No Stress”
text: "No Stress" is a 2008 song recorded by the French house record producer and DJ Laurent Wolf. It was the first single from his sixth album Wash My World, on which it features as the first track in its radio edit version, and as the tenth track in the Zen @ Acoustic version.

title: “Tired of Being Sorry”
text: "Tired of Being Sorry" is a song written by American singer-songwriter Scott Thomas for his band, Ringside. It was a big radio hit in Poland in 2005.

title: “Rayon de soleil”
text: "Rayon de soleil" is the name of a 2008 song recorded by the African singer William Baldé. It was his debut single and was released in July 2008 from his album En Corps étranger.

title: “Dégénération”
text: "Dégénération" is a 2008 song by French singer-songwriter Mylène Farmer. It was the first single from her seventh studio album Point de Suture, and was released first digitally and on radio in June 2008, then in a CD in August 2008.

title: “Beggin'”
text: "Beggin'" is a song composed by Bob Gaudio and Peggy Farina and first released as a single by American band the Four Seasons in 1967. Initially charting at number 16 on the US Billboard chart, the song became popular in the Northern soul scene in the United Kingdom in the 1970s.

title: “Infinity 2008”
text: "Infinity", also known as "Infinity", is a song by British acid house musician Guru Josh.

title: “Appelle mon numéro”
text: "Appelle mon numéro" is a 2008 song recorded by French singer Mylène Farmer. Released on 3 November 2008, it was the second single from her seventh studio album, Point de Suture.

title: “Ça n'finira jamais”
text: "Ça n'finira jamais" is a 2008 song recorded by French artist Johnny Hallyday. It was the first single from his album of the same name on which it features as first track.

title: “Womanizer”
text: "Womanizer" is a song by American singer Britney Spears from her sixth studio album, Circus. It was released on September 26, 2008, by Jive Records as the lead single of the album.
